English | 中文
# dsh-toolset
An in-process plugin toolset for DSH (DeepSeek Harness): a set of TypeScript plugins mounted into th
e DSH session process as cordis bundles, filling in capabilities such as task trees, a knowledge bas
e with persistent memory, goal contracts, and metric loops. It also ships a homegrown terminal UI (T
UI) — a third way to interact with DSH alongside the Web UI and the CLI.
For agent-facing collaboration rules, see `AGENTS.md` in the repository root. For DSH contract notes
shared across plugins, see `docs/host/DSH-CTX-API.md` (read-only reference; last clause-by-clause r
eview against `dsh-v0.1.7-rc.2`; the `0.2.1-rc.2` / `0.2.1-rc.3` / `0.2.1-rc.5` comparisons found no
change on the surfaces this project consumes, while `0.2.2-rc.1` changes several of them — see `doc
s/host/HOST-UPGRADE-0.2.2-rc.1.md` (previous: `docs/host/HOST-UPGRADE-0.2.1-rc.5.md`)).
## Composition
The repository contains the `TUI/` terminal UI package and 37 in-process plugins, all standalone npm
packages (`@dsh-toolset/*`):
| Package | What it does |
| **TUI** (`TUI/`, `@dsh-toolset/tui`) | Terminal UI: four-region layout (conversation / activity /
status column / input), event-driven rendering, slash commands, session switching and cleanup, model
and approval panels; **zero third-party runtime dependencies** (no third-party imports in the sourc

e, only the repo's `clock-base` clock probe helper is reused, colors via manual ANSI) |
| **clock-ba
se** | Timer unification surface: the `clock` service (`now()` plus `scope(ctx)` returning `schedule
(delayMs, cb)` / `interval(delayMs, cb)`, whose disposal is registered on the caller's `ctx.effect`
so a plugin unload leaves no live timer; handles are `unref`ed by default). Also exports a hand-driv
en `ManualClock` (advance the clock, fire due callbacks in order) for tests. Coexists with, and does
not wrap, the host's `cordis-plugin-timer`: no `schedule`, no `unref`, and a required `inject` make

wrapping a worse deal |
| **herdr-integration** | herdr panel bridge: agent state is reported to th
e herdr panel over a unix socket, and blocked events are bridged across three signal sources (ask-us

er questions, approvals, turn blocking) |
| **herdr-use** | Terminal read/write over herdr: ten mode
l-facing tools `herdr_list` / `herdr_read` / `herdr_info` / `herdr_wait` / `herdr_create` / `herdr_c
lose` / `herdr_label` / `herdr_text` / `herdr_key` / `herdr_run` (no `action` parameter); a terminal
= one tab plus its own root pane, and `terminal_id` is that root pane id, so the model never deals
with panes, tabs or workspaces; the foreground lane inherits the parent herdr session, the backgroun
d lane lives in a `dshbg` session and starts that headless server on demand; each dsh session is str
ictly bound to one workspace per lane; it also provides the `herdrUse` service surface to other in-p
rocess plugins, sharing the same registry and the same write lock as the tools; write tools pass thr

ough the read-only sandbox gate and security-guard registration |

## Quick start (build and test)
The repository root `package.json` delegates to all subpackages:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`test:smoke` delegates to `scripts/run-smoke.sh`: it keeps `DSH_HOME`, `TMPDIR` and logs under the r
epo `tmp/`, so the smokes work inside a sandbox (they never write `~/.dsh`). The model defaults to t
he local tollgate gateway (`TOLLGATE_API_KEY=local`, provider `tollgate`, model `qwen38`); override
with `TOLLGATE_API_KEY` / `TOLLGATE_BASE_URL` / `SMOKE_PROVIDER` / `SMOKE_MODEL`.
Inside a single subpackage you can run its own `pnpm run check / build / test / demo` directly (the
TUI also has `bench` and `smoke:pty`). For command details, parallel scheduling flags and filter usa
ge, see `AGENTS.md`.
## Wiring into a DSH profile
One-shot install on a new machine (install dsh → build all plugins → create a profile mounting 38 pa
ckages: TUI + 37 plugins):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
One run produces **two** profiles that differ only in how plugins are linked:
| profile | dependency | picks up repo changes | use |
| `fff` (main) | `file:` snapshot | no; rerun `scripts/install.sh --profile fff --sync` | running se

ssions, acceptance runs |
| `fff-test` | `link:` symlink | immediately after `pnpm run build` | live
development in a new window |
The main profile is installed as a real copy: pnpm would hard-link `file:` directory dependencies, s
o the script copies each plugin once more to break those links (in-place rewrites in the repository,
e.g. `tsc` output, would otherwise leak into the profile through the shared inode). Refreshing it w
orks because the script drops pnpm's "already up to date" markers before installing — pnpm does not
track the content of `file:` directories (measured). The companion profile reuses the main profile's
finished `dsh.profile.bundles`, `cordis.patch.yml` and `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (the last one copied w
ith the copy-mode overrides block stripped, which would otherwise pin nested `link:` dependencies to
`file:` snapshots), with dependency values rewritten to `link:`. `--no-test-profile` installs the m
ain profile only, `--profile-test <name>` renames the companion, and `--mode link` makes the main pr
ofile symlink-based too.
[该节后续省略]
### Agent-side composition (no preset)
This project uses the TUI only, and the agent side comes from the profile's global composition (`dsh
-base` + this project's bundles + `cordis.patch.yml`). **No agent preset is configured or loaded**:
in the official design the TUI is "a single composition surface without a preset", so `/preset` repo
rting that the agent preset service is unavailable is expected. To change tools, prompts or persona,
put it in the profile user patch; for multiple compositions, use multiple profiles. See `docs/host/
AGENT-COMPOSITION.md` for the official basis, local verification, and the 0.1.7 version gap.
## Documentation
This is the only index (`AGENTS.md` does not repeat the list); each maintained document opens with t
hree lines stating "what it owns / what it does not own / when it expires".
Two change flows: `docs/WORKFLOW-STANDARD.md` (standard) and `docs/WORKFLOW-FAST.md` (small changes)
, with the short form in `AGENTS.md`.
**Project-level (`docs/`)**
- `docs/ROADMAP.md` — future development directions and completion criteria (progress, schedule and

items live in `docs/BACKLOG.md` §3 milestones).
